subject: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, break-glass
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintrust.com>
Cc: FinTrust Security Team <security@fintrust.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: access controls & support access (post-call recap)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few follow-ups on access controls so your security team can review: 

1) RBAC surface
   - Redwood supports role-based access control with customizable roles and attribute-based filters.
   - Default roles: Admin, Engineer, ReadOnly, Support. Customers can create scoped roles limited to projects/models.

2) Least privilege & segregation
   - Token scoping and route-level permissions (can restrict token to embeddings-only, generation-only).
   - Environment-level separation for dev/staging/prod.

3) Support access / break-glass
   - Support access is by default not enabled; it must be allowed per-account with explicit approvals.
   - Break-glass requires multi-party approval (customer SSO admin + Redwood on-call) and is logged + time-limited.

4) Logging & retention
   - Detailed audit logs (user actions, admin changes, support sessions) retained by default for 90 days; configurable up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private deployments.

5) Data residency
   - Hosted data regions: us, eu, apac. Option to pin region at account level. Private deployment available for on-prem/VPC.

Attached: redwood_rbac_practices.pdf and an access-controls checklist we promised.

Next steps I mentioned on the call: 
- Please confirm the FinTrust requirements for support access (e.g., who can approve break-glass, retention thresholds).
- If useful, we can schedule a 45-min security deep-dive with our product security lead next week.

Would you be able to send over the team’s minimum spec (break-glass workflow, required retention period for logs, and any required audit evidence)? I can map those to our controls and highlight any gaps.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team before we share the formal spec: 

1) Break-glass: can you confirm the exact process and approvals required on Redwood’s side? Is SSO + 2-person Redwood approval enforced?
2) Support sessions: are they interactive sessions with timeboxed temporary credentials, and are session recordings/audit logs exported to the customer?
3) Least privilege: can you provide an example of a scoped role that allows only model inference (no model upload or billing visibility)?

We’ll compile the formal retention and audit requirements, but want to make sure we understand Redwood’s default behavior so we can spot any gaps.

—Jane
Jane Doe
Security Manager, FinTrust
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fintrust.com>
Cc: FinTrust Security Team <security@fintrust.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: access controls & support access (post-call recap)

Hi Jane —

Great questions — answered inline below and I’ve attached the two docs for your security team to review. Happy to pull our Product Security lead into the deep-dive.

1) Break-glass process:
   - Customer initiates a break-glass request via the Console or API.
   - Requires customer SSO admin approval + one Redwood on-call engineer sign-off.
   - Once approved, access is time-limited (default 2 hours) and elevated privileges are scoped to only the resources required.
   - All actions during break-glass are audited and immutable in the audit log.

2) Support sessions:
   - Support access is provided via short-lived, audited sessions (temporary credentials).
   - Sessions can be recorded/keystroke-logged if the customer opts in; recordings and session logs can be exported via S3 to a customer-controlled bucket.
   - We also provide a session transcript and the exact API calls made during the support session.

3) Scoped role example (inference-only):
   - Role: fintrust_inference_operator
   - Permissions: call_inference, read_model_metadata, no write_model, no billing_view, no admin_console.
   - Can be created via the Console or Terraform provider; I’ve included a snippet in the attached redwood_rbac_practices.pdf.

Additional notes:
- Audit log retention: Hosted default 90 days; for Dedicated/Private customers we can support 7-year retention with archival to a pinned region.
- Data residency: We can pin your account to the us-east region and provide isolated storage.

Attachments: redwood_rbac_practices.pdf; access-controls-checklist.xlsx

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm you want a security deep-dive, Rishi (cc’d) can join and demo the console + show audit/export flow.
- Please send the minimum required retention period and any required evidence types (e.g., session recordings, audit entries with user IDs).

I’ll also prepare a short mapping doc showing how each FinTrust requirement maps to Redwood controls.

Best,
Marissa
